moduleTitle: Identifying CLI prerequisites in Tricentis Testim
learningObjectives: Identify what must be installed on a machine before the Testim CLI can run.
Explain which Node.js versions the Testim CLI supports.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: What the CLI needs to run

elements.description: Running Testim via the CLI requires Node.js to be installed on the machine — the CLI is itself an npm package and runs in the Node.js runtime.
Testim supports all LTS (Long-Term Support) / supported versions of Node.js — not just one specific pinned version — giving teams flexibility in which supported Node.js release they standardize on.

The CLI requires its installed package and supported Node.js on the initiating machine. Local/grid execution additionally needs its own browser/device infrastructure, credentials and connectivity; runtime prerequisites alone do not establish readiness.

elements.term: The Testim CLI package itself also has a version-support policy
elements.description: The CLI prerequisites table specifies latest CLI with backward compatibility for the previous two versions. It also lists a Node.js supported-runtime requirement with a previous-two compatibility comment. The table does not define those as previous major releases or guarantee end-of-life Node.js security/support.

elements.text: Check upstream Node.js release status and the installed CLI’s compatibility. Current, Active LTS, Maintenance LTS and End-of-Life are different statuses; a previously LTS line can be end-of-life today.

bulletPoints: Prerequisite: Node.js installed (the CLI is an npm package).
Check currently supported runtime status and installed CLI compatibility, rather than relying on an old LTS label.
Once installed, the CLI can trigger local or remote runs.
The Testim CLI package itself: latest version supported, plus backward compatibility for the previous two versions.
For the current Node.js LTS list, Testim's docs point to github.com/nodejs/Release.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming the CLI requires one exact Node.js version
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Blocking a CI pipeline upgrade because of a belief that only one specific Node.js version is compatible with the Testim CLI.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Testim supports all LTS/supported versions of Node.js, not a single pinned version — there's flexibility in which supported release a team standardizes on.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What must be installed on a machine before the Testim CLI can be used?

options.text: Nothing — the CLI has no prerequisites.

practiceQuiz.hint: The CLI is distributed as an npm package.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Running via CLI requires Node.js installed, since the Testim CLI is itself an npm package that runs in the Node.js runtime.

optionExplanations.A: The npm CLI runs on Node.js.
optionExplanations.B: A JDK is not the stated underlying CLI runtime.
optionExplanations.C: Python is not the stated npm CLI runtime.
optionExplanations.D: The CLI has documented runtime prerequisites.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which Node.js versions does the Testim CLI support?

options.text: Only Node.js version 14, and no others.
Node.js is not required or used at all.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's a range, tied to Node.js's own support lifecycle.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Testim supports all LTS/supported versions of Node.js, giving flexibility rather than pinning to one exact version.

optionExplanations.A: The current requirement is not restricted to obsolete Node 14.
optionExplanations.B: The CLI guide refers to LTS/supported runtime versions; verify current upstream status.
optionExplanations.C: Experimental-only builds are not the documented requirement.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Besides Node.js, what else does Testim maintain a version-support policy for?

options.text: Nothing — only the Node.js version matters.
The Testim CLI package itself: the latest version is supported, with backward compatibility for the previous two versions.
The version of the CI platform being used, not the CLI.

practiceQuiz.hint: The npm package you install also has its own support window.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Testim CLI npm package itself has a version-support policy: the latest version is supported, with backward compatibility maintained for the previous two versions — this is separate from, and in addition to, the Node.js version requirement.

optionExplanations.A: The installed CLI package also has a compatibility statement.
optionExplanations.B: The prerequisites table includes this CLI compatibility statement.
optionExplanations.C: CI platform versioning is not a substitute for CLI compatibility.
optionExplanations.D: Browser compatibility is separate from the CLI package statement.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What backward-compatibility count does the CLI prerequisites table state for prior CLI versions, without specifying major-release granularity?

options.text: None — only the very latest version works.

practiceQuiz.hint: The table says previous two versions; it does not define them as major releases.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The table states previous two versions alongside latest CLI. It does not establish a previous-two-major-release policy or override upstream Node.js end-of-life status.

optionExplanations.A: The table mentions compatibility beyond latest.
optionExplanations.B: The table says previous two versions, without major-release granularity.
optionExplanations.C: It does not promise every historic version remains supported.
optionExplanations.D: The stated count is two, not one.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Where does Testim's documentation direct you to check the exact, current list of Node.js LTS/supported versions?

options.text: The official Node.js Release repository on GitHub (nodejs/Release).
It doesn't provide any reference — you must guess.

practiceQuiz.hint: Testim defers to Node.js's own upstream source of truth rather than duplicating it.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Rather than pinning a static version list that would quickly go stale, Testim's docs point to the official Node.js Release repository on GitHub (nodejs/Release) as the source of truth for current LTS/supported versions.

optionExplanations.A: The guide links upstream release status, not solely its changelog.
optionExplanations.B: The official upstream repository publishes the release lifecycle.
optionExplanations.C: Community chat is not the linked authoritative schedule.
optionExplanations.D: The documentation supplies an upstream reference.

quickRecap.value: Node.js must be installed — the CLI is an npm package.
Check current Node.js release status and CLI compatibility; historic LTS labels do not imply current support.
The table states latest CLI plus previous two versions, without defining major-release granularity.
